problem: Prove a variance-scaled lower bound on the Turán deficit at the first descent of a Poisson-binomial probability mass function.
debate: The literature on log-concavity and Turán-type inequalities for Poisson-binomial distributions, including bounds from Newton's inequalities and ultra-log-concavity.
gap: Existing lower bounds on the Turán deficit δk depend on the number of summands, individual success probabilities, or index k alone, and degenerate under variance-preserving parameter changes; no variance-scaled bound is known.
contribution: The paper proves V δD ≥ 1/4 at the first descent (tight between 1/4 and 1/3), derives variance-scaled inequalities at all indices and the rightmost mode, shows O(1/log N) bounds for random unitary matrices versus O(1/N) from ultra-log-concavity, and reduces the proof to exact arithmetic via Bernstein expansions.
note: Novel variance-scaled result with explicit gap analysis and applications to random matrices; a technical contribution appropriate for peer review.
